criteria: Recognize all 33 printed uppercase/lowercase pairs from letter-name or partner-form prompts without a model.
Distinguish Е/Ё, И/Й and Ь/Ъ; reject Latin lookalikes when a Cyrillic symbol is requested.
Identify the vowel carrying the teaching stress mark and distinguish the mark from an alphabet letter.
Copy each of the 66 printed letter forms with the requested case, using Cyrillic rather than Latin characters.
Retain the dots in Ё/ё, the breve in Й/й and the distinction between the two signs.
Copy a supplied vowel-plus-stress-mark sequence without omitting or detaching the accent.
Match all ten taught greeting and response expressions to their English meanings or written situations.
Distinguish greeting, farewell, thanks, courtesy and yes/no responses.
Write a taught greeting and farewell from situation cues without copying a displayed Russian model.
Write thanks, a suitable courtesy response and the taught yes/no forms with correct Cyrillic spelling.
Match the five taught subject pronouns to their intended reference, including familiar versus polite or plural you.
Recognize both taught names, the name label, the fixed naming question and the first-person introduction.
Write a minimal self-introduction using one taught name and either the no-copula pattern or the fixed naming expression.
Write the taught polite naming question without inventing new inflected forms.
Match the three taught written task instructions and the word/letter labels to their meanings.
Recognize all five taught clarification chunks in a text exchange.
Write the fixed non-understanding expression and a suitable taught repeat, explain or help request.
Complete the reading and repetition models with the correct taught command and polite expression.
Match all nine taught person/object nouns and the identification word to their meanings.
Interpret the book-identification model without mistaking это for an agreeing modifier.
Write the taught book-identification model and another identification using a taught nominative noun.
Keep это unchanged and use correct Cyrillic spelling and sentence punctuation.
Match each of the ten printed digits 0 through 9 to the corresponding taught Russian number word.
Interpret the supplied identification models for the printed digits 0 and 5 without introducing counted nouns.
Write every taught number word from its digit cue and write every digit from its Russian word cue.
Use the taught citation forms; preserve the soft signs and spell four, eight and nine correctly.
